# Kestravane Fleet - Price List

Version 4.2 - Effective 1 July 2026 - Supersedes all 3.x price lists

Approved by: Odalys Brennecke, VP Revenue Operations. Document owner: Deal Desk (dealdesk@kestravane.example).

All amounts in US dollars. For use by Kestravane account teams and authorised resellers in North America. Prices exclude sales tax.

## 1. Subscription plans

| Plan | Annual billing | Monthly billing | Minimum fleet |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launch | $29 per vehicle per month, billed annually | $35 per vehicle per month, billed monthly | Minimum 10 vehicles |
| Operations | $47 per vehicle per month, billed annually | $55 per vehicle per month, billed monthly | Minimum 25 vehicles |
| Enterprise | $72 per vehicle per month, billed annually | Not offered, annual contracts only | Minimum 150 vehicles |

A vehicle is any powered asset carrying an active TrakNode unit. Trailers and other unpowered assets are billed at $11 per asset per month on any plan.

A fleet smaller than the plan minimum may still subscribe to that plan, but it is billed for the minimum fleet size. Vehicles added during a term are prorated to the end of the term at the contracted rate.

Annual billing is invoiced upfront on Net 30 terms. Monthly billing is charged to a card on the first of each month and can be cancelled with one full billing cycle of written notice.

The contracted rate is locked for the length of the term. At renewal, increases on annual contracts are capped at 6% per year.

## 2. Optional modules

Modules can be added to any plan and are billed on the same cycle as the plan.

| Module | Price | Requires |
|---|---|---|
| Driver Safety Scoring | $6 per vehicle per month | TrakNode T4 |
| Fuel & Idle Analytics | $4 per vehicle per month | TrakNode T4 |
| Maintenance Planner | $5 per vehicle per month | Nothing further |
| Cold Chain Monitoring | $3 per sensor per month | TempSense S2 sensors |
| Extended Video Retention | $8 per camera per month | RoadLens camera |

## 3. Add-ons and services

| Item | Price | Availability |
|---|---|---|
| NetSuite connector | $400 per month | Enterprise only |
| Technical Account Manager | $18,000 per year | Enterprise only |
| Assisted data migration | $1,500 one-time | Operations; included in the Enterprise onboarding fee |
| On-site training day | $1,400 per day plus travel | Operations, Enterprise |
| Sandbox environment | $150 per month | Operations; included on Enterprise |

Availability of the other native connectors by plan is published in the Integration Matrix.

## 4. Onboarding fee

The onboarding fee is charged once, on the first invoice.

| Plan | Onboarding fee |
|---|---|
| Launch | No fee, self-serve setup |
| Operations | $2,500 one-time |
| Enterprise | $7,500 one-time |

The fee covers the kickoff call, account configuration, two remote admin training sessions and support through go-live. It does not cover hardware installation.

## 5. Hardware

Hardware is purchased outright and is invoiced on shipment.

| Item | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| TrakNode T4 telematics unit | $89 per unit | One required per vehicle |
| TempSense S2 temperature sensor | $64 per sensor | Wireless, pairs with a TrakNode |
| RoadLens dual-facing camera | $229 per camera | Road and cab view |
| Professional installation | $45 per vehicle | Covers every device fitted in the same visit |

Self-installation carries no charge. Shipping within the contiguous United States is free on orders of 20 units or more; smaller orders ship for $75 flat. All hardware carries a 3-year warranty with advance replacement.

## 6. Discounts

Discounts apply to plan subscription fees only. Modules, add-ons, hardware, installation and onboarding fees are never discounted.

### 6.1 Volume discount

The volume discount is applied automatically on annual billing. Monthly billing is not eligible.

| Fleet size under contract | Discount off list |
|---|---|
| 100 to 249 vehicles | 5% volume discount |
| 250 to 499 vehicles | 8% volume discount |
| 500 or more vehicles | 12% volume discount |

### 6.2 Approval authority

The thresholds below refer to the total discount off list, with the volume discount counted in.

| Total discount | Who may approve |
|---|---|
| Up to 10% | Account Executive, no further approval needed |
| Above 10%, up to 18% | Regional Sales Director |
| Above 18%, up to 25% | VP Sales, after Deal Desk review |
| Above 25% | Not available without a written exception from the CFO |

A quote that exceeds the signer's authority is not valid until the approval is recorded in the Deal Desk queue. Committing to a three-year term locks the rate for the whole term but does not add a further percentage discount.

### 6.3 Pilots and special schedules

A 21-day pilot of up to 5 vehicles, with hardware on loan, can be offered with sign-off from the Regional Sales Director. Municipal and non-profit fleets are quoted from the Public Sector schedule, which is maintained separately.

## 7. Plan highlights

| Plan | Support channels | Customer success | Uptime commitment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launch | Email | Help centre | None |
| Operations | Email and chat | Pooled Customer Success team | Yes |
| Enterprise | Phone, email and chat | See note below | Yes |

Enterprise fleets of 250 or more vehicles are assigned a named Customer Success Manager; smaller Enterprise fleets are served by the pooled Customer Success team.

Full support terms, response targets and uptime figures are set out in the Support Plans and Service Level Guide.

---

Kestravane, Inc. - Confidential. This price list replaces every earlier version on its effective date. Printed copies are uncontrolled.

# Kestravane Fleet - Integration Matrix

Edition 2026-Q3 - Effective 1 July 2026 - Published together with price list version 4.2

Approved by: Teodric Vanterpool, Director of Partner Engineering. Maintained by Partner Engineering; corrections to integrations@kestravane.example.

This matrix lists every integration Kestravane ships and supports, the plans on which each is available, and any fee. An integration that does not appear here is not supported.

## 1. Summary

| System | Type | Data direction | Plans | Fee |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Salesforce (Sales Cloud and Service Cloud) | Native connector | Two-way | Operations, Enterprise | Included at no additional charge |
| HubSpot | Native connector | One-way, Kestravane to HubSpot | Operations, Enterprise | No connector fee |
| NetSuite | Native connector | Two-way, standard records only | Enterprise only | $400 per month add-on |
| Slack | App | Outbound alerts | Launch, Operations, Enterprise | No fee |
| Microsoft Teams | App, in beta | Outbound alerts | Operations, Enterprise | No fee during beta |
| QuickBooks Online | Export | One-way invoice export | Launch, Operations, Enterprise | No fee |
| WEX fuel cards | Data feed | Inbound transactions | Operations, Enterprise | No fee |
| REST API and webhooks | Developer access | Read and write | Operations, Enterprise | No fee |

None of the native connectors is available on the Launch plan.

## 2. Connector detail

### 2.1 Salesforce

The Salesforce connector is part of the Operations and Enterprise subscriptions and carries no connector fee. It keeps Accounts, Contacts, Cases and Work Orders in step with Kestravane customers, sites and jobs, in both directions, on a 15-minute sync cycle. Custom fields on those standard objects can be mapped, up to 40 mapped fields per object. Salesforce custom objects can be mapped on Enterprise only, with a ceiling of 5 custom objects. The customer needs Salesforce Enterprise Edition or higher, or Professional Edition with API access enabled. One Salesforce org can be connected per Kestravane account.

### 2.2 HubSpot

The HubSpot connector posts vehicle visits, completed jobs and delivery exceptions to the company timeline in HubSpot once an hour. It is one-way: nothing written in HubSpot flows back into Kestravane. HubSpot Professional or higher is required.

### 2.3 NetSuite

The NetSuite connector exchanges five standard record types: Customer, Vendor, Item, Invoice and Purchase Order. It runs as a nightly batch, with an on-demand sync button for administrators. Custom records, custom segments and any other custom objects are not supported by the connector. Customers who depend on custom records build that part themselves against the REST API, usually with their own SuiteScript or through an implementation partner. There is no committed date for custom record support.

### 2.4 Slack and Microsoft Teams

The Slack app sends four kinds of alert to channels the customer chooses: geofence entry and exit, maintenance due, temperature excursion and harsh-driving events. Up to 25 channels can be connected. It does not accept commands typed in Slack. The Microsoft Teams app offers the same alerts but is in beta; beta features fall outside the uptime commitment and may change without notice.

### 2.5 REST API and webhooks

The REST API uses JSON over HTTPS with OAuth 2.0 client credentials. It is included on Operations and Enterprise and is not available on Launch.

| Plan | API rate limit |
|---|---|
| Operations | 600 requests per minute |
| Enterprise | 2,400 requests per minute |

Webhooks are available for trip completed, geofence, alert raised and device offline events. There is no GraphQL endpoint and no bulk export endpoint; bulk extracts are delivered as scheduled CSV files.

## 3. Systems without a connector

No native connector exists for the systems below, and none is planned for 2026. They can be reached through the REST API by the customer's own developers or by an implementation partner.

- SAP S/4HANA
- Microsoft Dynamics 365
- Sage Intacct
- QuickBooks Desktop
- Comdata fuel cards

## 4. General limitations

- Connectors are configured once, during implementation; each connects to a single production instance of the other system.
- Field mappings are changed by an account administrator in the admin console. Kestravane support does not edit mappings on a customer's behalf.
- Sync history is kept for 45 days for troubleshooting.
- Connector behaviour against a customer's sandbox of the other system is supported, but a Kestravane sandbox environment is needed for it.
- Partner-built integrations listed in the partner directory are supported by the partner, not by Kestravane.

---

Kestravane, Inc. This matrix describes shipped functionality on its effective date. It is not a roadmap and it creates no obligation to deliver functionality that is not listed.

# Kestravane Fleet - Security and Compliance Overview

Version 2026.2 - 12 June 2026

Owner: Ingrid Solheimsvik, Head of Security and Trust. Approved for sharing with customers and prospects. Reports referred to below are released under a non-disclosure agreement through trust@kestravane.example.

## 1. Purpose

This overview summarises the main controls that protect customer data in the Kestravane Fleet service. Where something is planned or in progress rather than in place, it says so. It is not a complete list of controls, nor of the laws and standards Kestravane works to; anything not covered here should be raised with the Security and Trust team.

## 2. Hosting and data residency

Kestravane Fleet runs on Amazon Web Services.

| Region | Location | Availability |
|---|---|---|
| United States (default) | Oregon, with disaster recovery in Ohio | All plans |
| European Union | Frankfurt, Germany | Enterprise only |

The region is chosen when the account is provisioned. Moving an account between regions after go-live is not supported. No other hosting regions are available, and Kestravane does not offer an on-premises or customer-hosted deployment.

## 3. Encryption

Data at rest is encrypted with AES-256. Data in transit is protected with TLS 1.2 or higher; TLS 1.3 is used wherever the client supports it. Encryption keys are held in AWS Key Management Service and rotated every 12 months. Customer-managed encryption keys are not offered.

TrakNode units encrypt data before sending it over the cellular network, and each unit holds its own device certificate.

## 4. Identity and access

| Capability | Availability by plan |
|---|---|
| Single sign-on (SAML 2.0 or OpenID Connect) | Included on Operations and Enterprise; not available on Launch |
| SCIM 2.0 user provisioning | Included on Enterprise only |
| Multi-factor authentication | Required for password logins on Launch; enforced through the identity provider on Operations and Enterprise |
| Role-based access control | 3 fixed roles on Launch; custom roles as well on Operations and Enterprise |

Single sign-on has been verified with Okta, Microsoft Entra ID, Google Workspace and Ping Identity. SCIM provisioning creates, updates and deactivates users and maps identity provider groups to Kestravane roles.

Kestravane staff reach production systems only through a bastion with hardware-key authentication, and access is reviewed every quarter.

## 5. Audit logs

Administrative actions and data-access events are written to an audit log that customers can read in the admin console.

| Plan | Audit log retention |
|---|---|
| Launch | 30 days |
| Operations | 90 days |
| Enterprise | 13 months |

Enterprise customers can also pull audit events into their own SIEM through the audit log API. Audit entries cannot be edited or deleted by customer administrators or by Kestravane staff.

## 6. Independent assurance

SOC 2: Kestravane holds a SOC 2 Type II report covering the period 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026, issued on 22 May 2026 by Harrowgate Assurance LLP. The report covers the Security and Availability trust services criteria. Confidentiality, Processing Integrity and Privacy are outside its scope.

ISO 27001: Kestravane is not ISO 27001 certified. The Stage 1 audit was completed in March 2026 and the Stage 2 audit is scheduled for November 2026. Certification is not expected before the first quarter of 2027, and no date is committed.

Penetration assessment: an external assessment of the web application, the API and the TrakNode firmware is carried out once a year. The most recent one was completed in February 2026 by Corvane Labs. A summary letter is available; the full report is not shared.

## 7. Data retention and deletion

| Data | Retention while the contract is active |
|---|---|
| Vehicle location and engine data | 25 months, then deleted; aggregated reports are kept |
| Temperature sensor readings | 36 months |
| Camera footage | 45 days, or 180 days with Extended Video Retention |
| Driver safety events | 25 months |

When a contract ends, the customer can export its data for 30 days after the termination date. All customer data is deleted from production systems within 60 days of the termination date, and from backups within a further 35 days.

## 8. Resilience

Production databases are backed up every day and replicated to the disaster recovery site. The recovery point objective is 24 hours and the recovery time objective is 8 hours. Recovery is rehearsed twice a year.

## 9. Privacy

Kestravane acts as a processor of customer data. A data processing addendum incorporating the EU Standard Contractual Clauses is available on request for any plan. The list of sub-processors is published on the trust page and customers are notified 30 days before a new sub-processor is added. Kestravane does not sell customer data and does not use it to train models offered to other customers.

## 10. Vulnerability management

Critical vulnerabilities are remediated within 7 days and high-severity ones within 30 days. Kestravane runs a private bug bounty programme. Security incidents affecting customer data are notified to the affected customer's security contact within 72 hours of confirmation.

---

This overview is descriptive. It does not amend any contract. Contractual security terms are those in the customer's signed agreement.

# Kestravane Fleet - Support Plans and Service Level Guide

Revision 3 - Effective 1 July 2026

Approved by: Marisol Achterberg, VP Customer Operations. This guide describes the standard support and service level terms attached to each subscription plan. It is referenced by the Master Subscription Agreement.

## 1. Support by plan

| Plan | Channels | Hours | Languages |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launch | Email and help centre | Monday to Friday, 8:00 to 18:00 Central | English |
| Operations | Email and chat | 24 hours a day, Monday to Friday | English, Spanish |
| Enterprise | Phone, email and chat | 24 hours a day, 7 days a week | English, Spanish, French |

Phone support is offered on Enterprise only. Operations customers who call the main line are asked to open a chat or email ticket.

## 2. Severity levels

- Priority 1: the service is unavailable, or vehicle data has stopped arriving for more than a quarter of the fleet.
- Priority 2: a major function is impaired and no workaround exists.
- Priority 3: a minor fault, a how-to request or a cosmetic problem.

The support engineer assigns the severity. A customer may ask for it to be reviewed by the duty lead.

## 3. First response targets

| Plan | Priority 1 | Priority 2 | Priority 3 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Launch | Priority 1: 4 business hours | Priority 2: 1 business day | Priority 3: 3 business days |
| Operations | Priority 1: 1 hour | Priority 2: 4 business hours | Priority 3: 1 business day |
| Enterprise | Priority 1: 30 minutes | Priority 2: 2 hours | Priority 3: 8 business hours |

These are targets for a first response from a support engineer, measured within the support hours of the plan. They are not resolution times and they carry no service credit.

## 4. Uptime

Uptime is measured per calendar month for the web application and the API, excluding scheduled maintenance.

| Plan | Monthly uptime commitment | Service credit |
|---|---|---|
| Launch | No commitment | None |
| Operations | 99.5% | 5% of the monthly subscription fee if uptime is below 99.5%; 10% if it is below 99.0% |
| Enterprise | 99.95% | 10% of the monthly subscription fee if uptime is below 99.95%; 25% if it is below 99.0% |

For annual contracts the monthly subscription fee is one-twelfth of the annual plan fee. A credit must be claimed in writing within 45 days of the end of the affected month and is applied to the next invoice; credits are not paid out in cash. Service credits are the sole remedy for missed uptime.

Scheduled maintenance takes place on Sundays between 02:00 and 05:00 Central, is announced 5 business days ahead, and is limited to 6 hours in any month. Beta features, the customer's own network and third-party systems on the other end of a connector are outside the uptime commitment.

## 5. Changes to standard terms

The uptime figures above are the only ones Kestravane offers. A different uptime figure, a different credit schedule or a response-time commitment in a contract is a non-standard term. Non-standard terms need written approval from the VP Customer Operations and from Legal, requested through Deal Desk, before they are put in front of a customer. Account teams must not offer or imply service levels other than those in this guide.

## 6. Customer success coverage

| Plan | Coverage |
|---|---|
| Launch | Help centre and email |
| Operations | Pooled Customer Success team, with a group check-in webinar each quarter |
| Enterprise, 300 or more vehicles | Named Customer Success Manager, with a business review each quarter |
| Enterprise, fewer than 300 vehicles | Pooled Customer Success team, with a business review twice a year |

A Technical Account Manager can be added to any Enterprise account as a paid add-on; see the price list.

## 7. Escalation

1. A Priority 1 ticket that is not resolved within 2 hours is escalated to the Duty Incident Manager.
2. At 4 hours the VP Customer Operations is notified and joins the incident channel.
3. Enterprise customers receive an update every hour during a Priority 1 incident; Operations customers every 4 hours.
4. Any customer can ask for an escalation at any time by replying "escalate" on the ticket or, on Enterprise, by calling the escalation line printed on the welcome letter.

Current incidents and maintenance notices are posted on status.kestravane.example.

## 8. Hardware returns

A TrakNode, sensor or camera that fails under warranty is replaced in advance: the replacement ships within 2 business days of the fault being confirmed, with a prepaid label for the faulty unit. Units damaged by collision, water ingress beyond the rated level or unauthorised opening are not covered.

## 9. What support does not cover

- Building or debugging the customer's own code against the API.
- Editing connector field mappings on the customer's behalf.
- On-site visits, which are quoted separately as training or professional services.

---

# Kestravane Fleet - Implementation and Onboarding Guide

Version 2.3 - 14 April 2026

Owner: Bartholomew Nkemelu, Director of Professional Services. Written for customers who are about to start a rollout and for the Kestravane teams who support them.

## 1. How a rollout runs

Every rollout moves through the same six stages: kickoff, configuration, hardware installation, data migration, training and go-live. On Launch the customer runs these stages alone with the setup wizard. On Operations a Kestravane onboarding specialist guides the customer through them. On Enterprise a named project manager runs the plan and chairs a weekly status call.

The kickoff call is normally held within 5 business days of contract signature. Every duration in this guide is counted from the kickoff call, not from the signature.

## 2. Typical timelines

| Plan and fleet size | Delivery model | Duration from kickoff to go-live |
|---|---|---|
| Launch | Self-serve | 5 to 10 business days |
| Operations, up to 200 vehicles | Guided | Typically 30 days |
| Operations, more than 200 vehicles | Guided | 45 to 75 days |
| Enterprise | Managed, with a named project manager | 60 to 90 days |

These durations are planning estimates drawn from completed projects. They are not commitments, and Kestravane does not write go-live dates into order forms. Where a customer needs a committed date, it is set out in a Statement of Work signed by the Director of Professional Services after a scoping call; account teams cannot commit to a date on their own.

The most common causes of delay are vehicles not being released for installation, a late vehicle list, and waiting for the customer's identity provider team to configure single sign-on.

## 3. What the rollout depends on

- Hardware delivery. Units arrive 7 to 10 business days after the hardware order is placed. Installation cannot be scheduled until the delivery date is confirmed.
- Installer availability. Professional installation is booked at least 10 business days ahead. One two-person installer crew fits about 15 vehicles per working day at a single depot.
- Vehicle downtime. A professional installation keeps a vehicle off the road for about 40 minutes. A self-installed TrakNode on a light vehicle with an OBD-II port takes about 20 minutes; heavy trucks need the 9-pin harness and are best left to an installer.
- Connectors. Each native connector takes 3 to 5 business days to configure and validate, and the customer's administrator for the connected system has to be available during that window.
- Single sign-on. The customer's identity provider team supplies the metadata and assigns users; allow one week.

## 4. Customer responsibilities

The customer is asked to:

1. Name a project lead within 3 business days of the kickoff call. The project lead needs authority over vehicle scheduling.
2. Supply the vehicle list (VIN, licence plate, home depot and vehicle class) in the Kestravane template at least 5 business days before the first installation date.
3. Release vehicles for installation on the agreed days. Vehicles that are not presented are rebooked at the next available slot.
4. Supply the driver roster, with a unique identifier for each driver.
5. Send its administrators to both remote training sessions, each lasting 90 minutes.
6. Sign off the go-live checklist.

## 5. Data migration

Kestravane can load data from an earlier system so that reports do not start from zero.

| Data | What can be migrated |
|---|---|
| Vehicles, drivers and depots | All records, from the Kestravane CSV templates |
| Trip and location history | The most recent 24 months only |
| Maintenance history | Up to 5 years, as service records |
| Driver safety scores | Cannot be migrated; scores are recalculated from new data |
| Camera footage | Cannot be migrated |

Files must be UTF-8 CSV in the Kestravane templates. Ready-made converters exist for exports from Dorrowick Telematics and Pennoway Fleet; exports from any other system are mapped by the customer into the templates. Trip history older than 24 months is not loaded under any plan, because the reporting engine does not index it.

Assisted data migration, in which the onboarding specialist maps and loads the files, is a paid service on Operations and is part of the onboarding fee on Enterprise; the price list gives the amount. Customers on Launch load their own files with the import wizard.

Tracking hardware from another supplier cannot be reused with Kestravane Fleet. Every vehicle needs a TrakNode unit.

## 6. Training

Two remote sessions for administrators are included with onboarding on Operations and Enterprise. Dispatcher and driver training is delivered through recorded modules in the help centre. On-site training is available as a paid day.

## 7. Go-live and hypercare

A rollout is declared live when 95% of contracted vehicles have reported data for three consecutive days, the administrators have completed training and the customer has signed the go-live checklist.

For 14 days after go-live the onboarding specialist or project manager stays assigned to the account and handles issues directly. After that hypercare period the account moves to the standard support channels for its plan.

## 8. Changes during a rollout

Adding vehicles, depots or connectors after kickoff is handled through a change note agreed between the customer's project lead and the onboarding specialist. Changes can move the go-live date; the specialist gives a revised estimate when the change note is raised.

# Customer story: Hollowmere Produce Logistics

How a refrigerated carrier cut idling and temperature claims across 212 trucks

Published February 2026 by Kestravane Marketing, with the agreement of Hollowmere Produce Logistics. Figures were supplied by Hollowmere.

## The customer

Hollowmere Produce Logistics is a family-owned refrigerated carrier based in Yakima, Washington. It moves fruit and vegetables from packing houses in the Yakima Valley to grocery distribution centres across the Pacific Northwest. The fleet is 212 refrigerated trucks running out of three depots, with about 260 drivers on the roster.

## The problem

Before Kestravane, Hollowmere tracked its trucks with a basic location service and logged trailer temperatures by hand at each stop. Two things were costing money. Drivers left engines running at docks and rest stops, and nobody could say how much. And when a retailer rejected a load for a temperature excursion, Hollowmere had no continuous record to show where in the journey the load had warmed up, so it usually accepted the claim.

"We were arguing about claims with a clipboard," says Wendeline Aukes, Director of Fleet Operations at Hollowmere. "We lost most of those arguments."

## What Hollowmere bought

Hollowmere runs the Operations plan with two modules: Fuel & Idle Analytics and Cold Chain Monitoring. Each truck carries one TrakNode unit and two TempSense sensors, one at the front of the box and one at the rear doors, which makes 424 sensors in all. Hollowmere did not take cameras or Driver Safety Scoring, and it does not use any of the native connectors; dispatch data moves in and out through scheduled CSV files.

Hollowmere's own maintenance staff fitted the hardware, depot by depot.

## What was measured

Hollowmere compared the six months from 1 March to 31 August 2025, the first full period with every truck reporting, against the same six months of 2024.

| Measure | March to August 2024 | March to August 2025 | Change |
|---|---|---|---|
| Average engine idling per truck per day | 73 minutes | 59 minutes | 19% lower |
| Fuel consumed per 100 miles | 16.4 gallons | 15.4 gallons | 6.1% lower |
| Temperature-related load claims | 41 claims | 17 claims | 24 fewer |
| Claims accepted without dispute | 33 claims | 6 claims | 27 fewer |

Hollowmere estimates that the lower fuel consumption was worth about $186,000 over the six months, at the diesel prices it actually paid. Its finance team puts the payback on hardware and first-year subscription at under 9 months.

## How the savings came about

The idle report ranks depots and drivers by minutes of idling per day. Depot managers reviewed it every Monday and spoke to the ten drivers at the top of the list. Aukes says most of the change came in the first eight weeks, once drivers knew the number was being looked at.

On the cold chain side, the temperature excursion alert tells the dispatcher within minutes when either sensor leaves the set range. In several cases the driver was able to fix a door seal or reset the refrigeration unit before the load was lost. Where a claim was still made, the continuous record showed whether the excursion had happened in transit or after delivery.

## What these figures do and do not show

- The figures come from Hollowmere's own records. They have not been audited by Kestravane or by a third party.
- There was no control group. The comparison is the same fleet against its own previous year.
- Hollowmere launched a driver coaching programme in April 2025, during the measured period. Part of the idling and fuel improvement is likely to be due to that programme, and the two effects cannot be separated.
- The dollar estimate depends on diesel prices in 2025 and on Hollowmere's routes. The percentage change in fuel consumed per 100 miles does not depend on fuel price.
- This is one refrigerated fleet in one region. Results for other fleets, vehicle types and climates will differ, and nothing here is a forecast or a promise of results.

## What comes next

Hollowmere is evaluating Maintenance Planner for its 2026 budget and has asked for trailer door sensors, which Kestravane does not currently make.

"The idle number gets the attention," says Aukes, "but the claims are what changed how our customers treat us."

# Kestravane Partner Program Guide

Program year 2026-27 - Version 2.0 - Effective 1 July 2026 - Replaces the 2025-26 program overview

Approved by: Leontyne Abernethy-Osei, Head of Partnerships. Maintained by Channel Operations (partners@kestravane.example). Written for Kestravane partners and for the account teams who work alongside them. All amounts in US dollars.

## 1. What the program is for

Kestravane sells Kestravane Fleet through its own account teams and through partners. This guide sets out who can be a partner, what each kind of partner does, how partners are paid, and how partners and the direct team stay out of each other's way. It applies to companies established in the United States and Canada.

The program year runs from 1 July to 30 June. The rates, thresholds and benefits below apply to the whole program year and are reviewed once a year. This guide explains the program; the partner agreement is the contract.

## 2. Partner types at a glance

| Partner type | What the partner does | Who contracts with the customer | How the partner is paid |
|---|---|---|---|
| Referral partner | Introduces a prospect, then steps back | Kestravane | A referral fee, paid once |
| Reseller | Sells Kestravane Fleet subscriptions to its own customers and bills them | The reseller | A resale margin on what it resells |
| Installation partner | Fits hardware to vehicles on Kestravane's behalf | Kestravane | A per-vehicle rate set out in the partner's installation schedule |

A company can be more than one kind of partner.

## 3. Referral partners

Any business that meets fleet operators can apply: insurance brokers, fuel suppliers, body builders, maintenance shops, consultants. There is no certification requirement and no revenue target. The partner accepts the referral agreement in the partner portal and can register introductions from that day.

The partner earns a referral fee of 9% of the plan subscription fees billed to the referred customer for its first twelve months, calculated after any discount. Fees for modules, add-ons, hardware, installation and onboarding are left out of the calculation. The fee is limited to $20,000 for any one referred customer.

The referral fee is paid once. Nothing further is paid on renewals, or on vehicles the customer adds after its first twelve months.

An introduction qualifies when:

- the prospect operates at least 12 vehicles;
- Kestravane has had no open opportunity with the prospect in the previous 9 months;
- the partner registered the introduction (section 5) before Kestravane's first meeting with the prospect; and
- the prospect becomes a paying customer while the registration is still protected.

The fee becomes payable once the customer has paid its first bill in full, and it appears on the partner's next quarterly statement. If the customer cancels or stops paying within its first 4 months the fee is forfeited, and a fee already paid is deducted from later statements.

## 4. Resellers

A reseller sells in its own name. It quotes from the Kestravane price list in force, takes the customer's order, bills the customer, and is billed in turn by Kestravane less its resale margin. A reseller has no discount authority of its own: any discount to an end customer follows the approval rules of the price list and is requested through the reseller's Partner Manager.

### 4.1 Tiers

| | Registered | Certified | Premier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Subscription revenue sourced in the previous program year | No minimum | $120,000 | $450,000 |
| Staff with the sales certification | 1 | 2 | 4 |
| Staff with the technical certification | None required | 1 | 3 |
| Resale margin on first-year subscriptions | 19% | 23% | 27% |
| Resale margin on renewals | 2% | 3% | 4% |
| Demo kits on loan | None | 2 kits | 6 kits |
| Co-marketing funds | Not available | Up to $6,500 a year | Up to $16,000 a year |
| Partner Manager | Channel desk | Named | Named, with a joint plan each quarter |

The resale margin is earned on plan subscription fees and on module fees, calculated after any discount. Hardware, installation, onboarding fees and add-on services carry no margin; the reseller passes them on at the listed price.

### 4.2 Moving between tiers

Tiers are set at the annual review in July, on the subscription revenue the reseller sourced in the program year just ended. A reseller that passes the next threshold during the year, and has the certified staff, can be promoted without waiting for the review; promotions are approved by the reseller's Partner Manager. A reseller that falls short at the review keeps its tier for the first half of the new program year and drops a tier at the half-year point if it has not caught up.

### 4.3 Certification

The sales certification is an online course of six modules with an examination; the pass mark is 80%. The technical certification adds a hands-on installation day at the Kansas City training bay and a workshop on the REST API. A certification belongs to the person, not to the company, and is valid for 18 months. The sales certification costs $350 per person and the technical certification $900 per person. Both are credited back to a reseller that reaches Certified within the same program year.

## 5. Deal registration

Every partner-sourced opportunity, referral or resale, starts with a registration in the partner portal. The partner gives the prospect's legal name, its depot addresses, an estimate of the fleet, the contact it is working with and the date of its last conversation.

An accepted registration is protected for 120 days from the date of acceptance. During that time no other partner can register the same prospect, and the direct team does not open a competing opportunity. If the prospect contacts Kestravane on its own while a registration is protected, the account executive brings the registering partner into the conversation.

Protection can be extended once, by 30 days, where the prospect has confirmed in writing that its evaluation is still running. Extensions are granted by the partner's Partner Manager. A registration with no logged activity for 60 days is closed, whether or not its protection has run out.

A registration is turned down when:

- Kestravane or another partner already has an open opportunity with the prospect, or had one in the previous 9 months;
- the prospect is on the direct named-account list published in the portal at the start of each quarter; or
- the prospect is already a Kestravane customer, in which case added vehicles are an expansion and not a new opportunity.

Channel Operations reviews registrations in the order in which they arrive.

## 6. Leads passed from Kestravane

Kestravane passes some of its own inbound enquiries to resellers. An enquiry from a fleet of fewer than 35 vehicles, in a state or province where a Certified or Premier reseller is active, is offered to those resellers in rotation. Registered resellers do not receive passed leads.

The reseller that accepts a passed lead makes first contact within four working days and records the outcome in the portal. A lead that is not contacted in that time goes back to the direct team and is not offered again. A passed lead earns the reseller its normal margin; it does not count as sourced revenue for the tier thresholds.

## 7. Working with the direct sales team

Account executives are paid the same commission on a partner-sourced deal as on a direct one, so no account executive gains by working around a partner. A reseller's registered opportunities are visible to the account executive for the territory, who joins customer meetings when the reseller asks and handles anything that needs Kestravane's approval, such as pricing off the list or a change to contract terms.

Partners do not make commitments on Kestravane's behalf. A partner has no authority to vary Kestravane's subscription terms, its service levels or its delivery dates, and nothing a partner tells a customer binds Kestravane unless Kestravane confirms it in writing.

## 8. Customers who buy through a reseller

A customer that buys through a reseller gets the same service as a customer that buys direct.

- Contract. The customer accepts Kestravane's subscription terms as part of the reseller's order form. The reseller bills the customer.
- Onboarding. Onboarding is delivered by Kestravane Professional Services, in the same way as for a direct customer on the same plan. Resellers do not run onboarding and do not quote go-live dates.
- Support. The customer contacts Kestravane support directly, through the channels and during the hours of its plan. The reseller is not a first line of support and is not expected to triage tickets.
- Service levels. The Support Plans and Service Level Guide applies to resold customers exactly as it does to direct customers. Where a service credit is due, Kestravane issues it to the reseller as a credit note, and the reseller must pass the whole amount on to the customer on its next bill.
- Renewals. The reseller manages the renewal conversation and earns the renewal margin for its tier for as long as it remains the customer's reseller.

## 9. Installation partners

Installation partners fit TrakNode units, sensors and cameras for customers who have ordered professional installation. Customers always book and pay for installation through Kestravane; an installation partner does not quote customers and does not bill them.

Every fitter sent to a customer site carries a Kestravane installer certificate, earned on a two-day course and renewed every 18 months. Work follows the current installation guide, and for each vehicle the fitter uploads the photographs that guide asks for before leaving the site.

If a fault traced to the installation appears within 28 days, the installation partner returns to put it right at its own cost. Installation partners carry their own liability insurance, with cover of at least $2 million per occurrence.

## 10. Co-marketing funds and demo kits

Co-marketing funds pay for activity that produces registered opportunities: a stand at a regional trade show, a customer breakfast, local advertising. The reseller sends a short plan to its Partner Manager before spending anything and claims the cost, with receipts, by the end of the quarter after the activity. The amounts in the tier table are annual ceilings, not entitlements, and money not claimed in the program year lapses.

A demo kit contains one TrakNode T4, one RoadLens camera, two TempSense S2 sensors and a bench power supply. Kits remain Kestravane's property and are for demonstrations on the partner's own bench or vehicles. They are not lent to prospects.

## 11. Statements and pipeline reviews

Each partner receives a statement in the portal during the first month of every quarter. It lists the referral fees that became payable, the margin on subscriptions billed, co-marketing claims paid and any deductions. A partner has until the end of that quarter to query a statement.

Premier resellers review their pipeline with their Partner Manager every month, Certified resellers every quarter. Registered resellers are reviewed once a year, at the annual review.

## 12. Enterprise opportunities

The Enterprise plan is always contracted by Kestravane directly. It is not resold, whatever the reseller's tier, because Enterprise customers negotiate contract terms that only Kestravane can agree.

A reseller can still register an opportunity that turns out to need Enterprise. When a reseller's registered opportunity closes on the Enterprise plan, the reseller earns a co-sell fee of 13% of the first-year plan subscription fees, calculated after any discount, in place of any resale margin. The co-sell fee is the same for Registered, Certified and Premier resellers. It is paid once; no margin and no further fee is paid when the customer renews.

The account executive leads an Enterprise opportunity from the point at which the plan is confirmed, and the reseller stays involved under a short joint account plan. Enterprise revenue counts towards the reseller's tier threshold at half its value.

Referral partners are unaffected by this section: a referral that closes on Enterprise earns the referral fee described in section 3.

## 13. Disputes and exceptions

Most overlaps are settled by the registration date. Where they are not, for example where two partners each claim to have introduced the same prospect, or where a partner contests a rejected registration or a named-account ruling, the matter goes to the Director of Channel Operations, Hyacinth Morgenroth. Her decision is final. Partner Managers do not rule on disputes that involve their own partners.

Exceptions to the rates in this guide, such as a margin outside the tier table for a strategic opportunity, need the written agreement of the Head of Partnerships before the reseller quotes.

## 14. Conduct, brand and customer data

- Partners describe themselves as a "Kestravane Partner" with their tier, and never as Kestravane. The partner badge may be used on websites and quotations; the Kestravane logo on its own may not.
- Partners do not bid on Kestravane brand terms in paid search.
- A partner has no access to a customer's Kestravane account unless one of the customer's administrators creates a user for it. Partner staff with such access act on the customer's instructions.
- Gifts and hospitality offered to a prospect are limited to $80 per person per occasion.

## 15. Leaving the program

Either side can end a partner's participation with 50 days' written notice. Margin on subscriptions already billed is unaffected. Customers of a departing reseller move to Kestravane direct, or to another reseller of their choice, at their next renewal. Referral fees that have already become payable are paid on the next quarterly statement.

A Registered reseller with no accepted registration for 9 consecutive months is set to inactive and loses portal access until it asks to be reinstated.

## 16. Contacts

| Role | Name | Covers |
|---|---|---|
| Partner Manager, West | Ignatius Brandvold | Pacific and Mountain states, British Columbia, Alberta |
| Partner Manager, Central | Marguerite Oyelowo-Finch | Central states, Manitoba, Saskatchewan |
| Partner Manager, East | Casimir Thorvaldsen | Eastern states, Ontario, Quebec, Atlantic Canada |
| Director of Channel Operations | Hyacinth Morgenroth | Registration policy, disputes, partner statements |
| Channel desk | partners@kestravane.example | Registered resellers, referral partners, portal access |

The channel desk is staffed on working days from 7:30 to 16:30 Mountain time.

# Kestravane Partner Program - Overview for New Partners

Program year 2025-26 - Issued 4 August 2025 by Channel Operations

Welcome to the Kestravane partner program. This overview goes to every new partner together with its portal login. It explains, in a few pages, how the program works for the program year that began in July 2025. The partner agreement you accepted is the contract; this overview is the practical companion to it. Questions go to your Partner Manager or to partners@kestravane.example.

## How partners earn

A partner can earn with Kestravane Fleet as a referral partner or as a reseller.

Referral partners introduce a fleet operator and leave the selling to us. A referral partner earns a referral fee of 11% of the plan subscription fees billed to the customer it introduced, for that customer's first twelve months. There is no ceiling on the fee. It is paid once, on the statement that follows the customer's first payment, and nothing is paid on renewals.

Resellers sell in their own name, bill their customers and keep a margin. The margin depends on the reseller's tier:

| | Registered | Certified | Premier |
|---|---|---|---|
| Subscription revenue sourced in the previous year | No minimum | $100,000 | $380,000 |
| Staff with the sales certification | 1 | 2 | 3 |
| Resale margin on first-year subscriptions | 20% | 24% | 28% |
| Resale margin on renewals | 3.5% | 3.5% | 3.5% |
| Demo kits on loan | None | 1 kit | 4 kits |
| Co-marketing funds | Not available | Not available | Up to $12,000 a year |

Margin is earned on plan subscription fees. Modules, hardware, installation and onboarding are passed on at the listed price and carry no margin this year.

Tiers are looked at once a year, in July. To move up you need the revenue in the table and the certified staff; your Partner Manager will tell you where you stand at any time. A reseller that drops below its threshold moves down a tier straight away at the July review.

Resellers quote from the Kestravane price list in force on the day of the quote. A reseller cannot agree a discount by itself; talk to your Partner Manager before you promise a customer anything off the list.

## Registering a deal

Register every opportunity in the partner portal as soon as you know it is real, and before you bring a Kestravane account executive into a meeting. We need the prospect's legal name, where its vehicles are based, a rough fleet size and the name of the person you are talking to. The prospect must run at least 8 vehicles.

A registration that Channel Operations accepts is protected for 150 days. While it is protected, no other partner can register the same prospect and our direct team will not open an opportunity of its own. Protection cannot be extended this year: if the customer has not ordered when the protection ends, register the opportunity again and it will be looked at afresh.

A registration with no logged activity for 70 days is closed. Please log your calls and meetings; it takes a minute and it keeps your protection alive.

We turn a registration down when the prospect is already a customer, or when we or another partner have had an open opportunity with it during the last 9 months.

## Your first ninety days

New partners who get going quickly tend to stay active. We suggest this order:

1. Complete the sales certification. It is an online course of four modules, the pass mark is 75%, and it costs $275 per person. This year a certification lasts 12 months.
2. Join the new-partner call. It runs on the first Tuesday of every month at 11:00 Mountain time and lasts under an hour.
3. Register your first opportunity. Your Partner Manager will go through it with you.
4. If you are Certified or Premier, order your demo kit from the portal. A kit holds a TrakNode, a camera and two temperature sensors with a bench power supply.
5. Add your company to the partner directory, with the states or provinces you cover.

## Getting help

| Region | Partner Manager |
|---|---|
| West of the Mississippi, and western Canada | Ignatius Brandvold |
| East of the Mississippi, and eastern Canada | Casimir Thorvaldsen |

Registered resellers and referral partners who have no named Partner Manager write to the channel desk at partners@kestravane.example. The desk answers on working days between 8:00 and 16:00 Mountain time.

For anything about a customer's live service, such as a unit that has stopped reporting, the customer should contact Kestravane support. Partners are not expected to handle support tickets.

## Statements

Twice a year, in the first weeks of July and of the new calendar year, we send each partner a statement of what it has earned: referral fees, margin on the subscriptions billed in the half-year, and co-marketing claims paid. If something looks wrong, tell your Partner Manager before the end of the following month.

## Marketing with us

You may call yourself a "Kestravane Partner" and show the partner badge with your tier on your website and on your quotations. Please do not use the Kestravane logo by itself, and do not bid on our brand name in paid search.

Premier resellers can claim co-marketing funds for events and local advertising that we have agreed beforehand. Send the plan first and the receipts afterwards; claims for the program year close on 31 July 2026.

Twice a year we publish a short partner newsletter with product news, a customer example and the dates of the next certification courses. The partner conference takes place in Denver each spring; Premier resellers receive two places, and other partners can buy places at cost.

## A few house rules

- Partners do not commit Kestravane to prices, dates or service levels. If a customer needs something in writing from Kestravane, ask your Partner Manager.
- Hardware is shipped by Kestravane to the customer's depots. Resellers do not hold hardware stock.
- Professional installation is booked through Kestravane, including for resold customers.
- Either side can leave the program with 30 days' written notice.
- A partner that stops answering its Partner Manager for a whole quarter is treated as having left, and its open registrations are released.

We are glad to have you with us. Your Partner Manager will be in touch during your first fortnight to set up an introduction call.

texts.SALES-REF-HARDWARE-INSTALL-2026:
# TrakNode T4 and RoadLens - Installation Guide

Revision C - 8 June 2026

Owner: Anselm Vukovich-Tran, Field Engineering Manager. Written for Kestravane-certified fitters and for customers who fit their own units. TempSense sensors have their own fitting sheet and are not covered here.

## 1. Before you start

Each TrakNode T4 comes in a carton with the unit, an adhesive mounting pad, four cable ties and the harness named on the order. The serial number is printed on the underside of the unit and on the carton. It has twelve characters and begins with KT4.

You will need a trim removal tool, side cutters, isopropyl wipes, and a web browser logged in to the installer page of the admin console.

Check the vehicle against the vehicle list before opening the dash: VIN, licence plate and vehicle group. A unit fitted to the wrong vehicle reports under the wrong name until somebody corrects the record.

Work with the ignition off and the keys out of the vehicle. Do not fit a unit while the vehicle is on a lift, on charge or being fuelled, and do not disconnect any airbag wiring to make room.

| | TrakNode T4 | RoadLens |
|---|---|---|
| Size | 94 x 61 x 24 mm | 108 x 66 x 38 mm |
| Weight | 78 g | 164 g |
| Power | 9 to 32 volts from the harness | From the camera port of the TrakNode |
| Antennas | Internal, cellular and satellite | None |
| SIM | Built in; nothing to insert | None |

## 2. Choosing the connection

The TrakNode reads vehicle data through the diagnostic connector and takes its power from the same place. Use the harness that matches the connector. The vehicle compatibility list gives the same information by vehicle group, with example models.

| Connector in the vehicle | Typical vehicles | Harness |
|---|---|---|
| OBD-II, 16-pin | Cars, vans and pickups | KH-16Y |
| 16-pin OBD-style connector carrying J1939 | Medium-duty cab-over trucks | KH-16J |
| 9-pin round, green | Heavy trucks from 2016 | KH-9G |
| 9-pin round, black | Heavy trucks before 2016, yard tractors | KH-9B |
| No diagnostic connector | Forklifts, plant, older vehicles | KH-3W three-wire kit |

Every harness except the three-wire kit is a Y-harness: the vehicle's own connector stays available for a workshop tool. The 9-pin harnesses come with a 1.5-metre lead, because the connector on a truck is often low on the kick panel and the unit sits higher up. The KH-16Y and the KH-16J look alike apart from the grey band on the KH-16J. Fitting the wrong one of the pair gives position but no engine data.

The plug-in OBD-II connection is supported on light vehicles from model year 2008 onward. A light vehicle older than that is fitted with the three-wire kit.

The three-wire kit takes constant power, ignition and ground from the fuse box, using the fuse taps supplied. With this kit the unit reports position, trips and ignition time, but it has no odometer, fuel level or fault codes from the vehicle.

## 3. Mounting the unit

1. Choose a position under the dash or behind a trim panel, with the label side facing up and no metal directly above it.
2. Keep the unit at least 8 cm from airbag modules and their wiring, and clear of the pedals and the steering column.
3. Clean the surface with a wipe, apply the pad, press the unit on for thirty seconds, and add two cable ties round a solid part of the dash frame.
4. Route the harness so that it is not stretched and cannot be kicked. Tie up the spare length; do not coil it round the unit.
5. Never mount the unit in the engine bay, in a door or on the outside of the vehicle.

On tractors with a metallised or heated windshield, mount the unit as far forward on the dash top as the trim allows.

Some vehicles need extra care:

- Leased and rented vehicles: use the pad and cable ties only. Do not drill, and do not cut any of the vehicle's own wiring.
- Vehicles that already carry the maker's own telematics module on the diagnostic connector: fit the Y-harness between the connector and that module, never in its place.
- Vehicles with a body builder's control box under the dash: keep the unit and its harness on the opposite side of the steering column.
- Right-hand-drive vehicles: the connector is usually mirrored. Follow the connector, not the picture in this guide.

## 4. Power, memory and sleep

The unit runs on a supply of 9 to 32 volts, so one model covers 12-volt and 24-volt vehicles. With the ignition off it sleeps and draws less than 3 milliamps. It wakes on ignition and on movement.

When the vehicle is out of cellular coverage the unit keeps recording. It stores up to 9 days of trip data and sends it when coverage returns; beyond that, the oldest data is overwritten first.

A small internal backup cell keeps the unit reporting for a short time after power is removed, long enough to send a "power removed" message with its position. The vehicle then shows as offline in the admin console. The backup cell cannot be replaced by the user.

## 5. Activation and checks

Open the installer page, choose the vehicle and enter or scan the serial number. Then:

1. Turn the ignition on. The network light should turn solid green within 2 minutes.
2. With the vehicle outdoors, wait for the position light. A first fix normally takes up to 3 minutes; later fixes take seconds.
3. Check that the installer page shows ignition, odometer and, where the vehicle supports it, fuel level.
4. Turn the ignition off and on again and confirm that the page records both events.
5. Drive the vehicle at least 500 metres and confirm that a trip appears.

The vehicle is marked "Fitted" on the installer page when every check has passed.

## 6. Status lights

| Light | Pattern | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Network (green) | Solid | Connected to the cellular network |
| Network (green) | Slow blink | Searching for a network |
| Network (green) | Off | No power, or the unit is asleep |
| Position (blue) | Solid | Position fix obtained |
| Position (blue) | Slow blink | Looking for satellites |
| Fault (amber) | Slow blink | No vehicle data: wrong harness, or the vehicle's protocol was not detected |
| Fault (amber) | Fast blink | Supply below 9 volts |
| Fault (amber) | Solid | Firmware update in progress; do not unplug |

The lights switch off 10 minutes after the ignition is turned on, so that they do not distract the driver. Press the recessed button once to show them again.

## 7. Firmware

Units leave the warehouse with firmware 4.4 or later. Updates arrive over the air and install with the ignition on. An update takes about 6 minutes, during which the amber light is solid. The unit keeps its previous firmware and goes back to it if an update fails. Neither the fitter nor the driver has to do anything.

## 8. Fitting a RoadLens camera

The RoadLens is powered from the camera port of the TrakNode T4 through the 3-metre camera cable packed with the camera, so the TrakNode is always fitted first. One RoadLens can be connected to each TrakNode.

1. Position the camera on the windshield on the passenger side of the mirror, inside the area swept by the wipers and outside any tinted band.
2. Its top edge should sit no more than 6 cm below the headliner, so that it does not intrude on the driver's view.
3. Clean the glass, peel the backing from the mount and press the mount on for one minute. Do not fit the mount to cold or wet glass; warm the glass with the cab heater first.
4. Run the cable along the headliner and down the A-pillar behind the trim, away from the curtain airbag, and plug it into the camera port.
5. On the installer page, open the camera view and turn the road lens until the horizon lies between the two guide lines. Tilt the cab lens until both seats are in the picture.
6. Finish with the alignment drive: at least 3 km at more than 50 km/h on a road with lane markings. The camera view shows "Aligned" when it is done.

A camera that has been moved, or a vehicle whose windshield has been replaced, needs the alignment drive again.

## 9. Common problems

| Symptom | Likely cause | What to do |
|---|---|---|
| Amber slow blink that does not clear | KH-16Y fitted where KH-16J is needed, or the connector is not fully home | Check the compatibility list and reseat the harness |
| Position but no odometer | Three-wire kit in use, or the vehicle does not send odometer | Normal with the three-wire kit; otherwise report the vehicle group to Field Engineering |
| Network light never solid | Unit under a metal panel, or vehicle underground | Move the unit and test outdoors |
| Vehicle offline overnight | The unit is asleep | Normal; it wakes on ignition |
| Camera view is black | Cable in the wrong port, or not latched | Reseat both ends |
| Trips split in two at fuel stops | Ignition was off for less than the trip gap setting | An account setting, not a fitting fault |

## 10. Finishing the job

Upload three photographs for each vehicle from the installer page: the unit in position, the harness at the connector, and the serial label. Refit all trim. Put the workshop-tool side of the Y-harness back where the original connector was, so that a mechanic finds it where expected. Tell the customer's project lead which vehicles on the day's list were not presented.

Customers who fit their own units follow the same steps and use the installer page with an administrator's login. The photographs are optional for them, but they are worth taking: they save a visit if a unit is reported faulty later.

Wipe the road lens and the cab lens with a dry microfibre cloth when the camera is fitted and whenever the windshield is cleaned on the inside. Solvent cleaners cloud the lens cover.

Faulty units go back through Kestravane support. A fitter never opens a unit.

Field Engineering: fieldeng@kestravane.example

# CNW 2140 Computer Networks

## Lecture 7: TCP congestion control

Dr. Oleska Brantigern, School of Computing, Tarnhollow University

Tuesday 29 September 2026. Slide deck v3, exported with presenter remarks.

---

### Slide 1. Where we are

- Lecture 6 treated the transport as a pipe that just works. Today we open the pipe.
- Flow control protects the receiver (rwnd). Congestion control protects the network (cwnd).
- A sender keeps at most min(cwnd, rwnd) of unacknowledged data in flight.
- Nobody tells the sender how much capacity the path has. It has to find out by probing.

Presenter remarks: open with the 1986 collapse story. Two sites 400 yards apart, throughput down from 32 kbit/s to 40 bit/s. That is why this lecture exists.

### Slide 2. House conventions for CNW 2140

- cwnd and ssthresh are counted in segments, never in bytes.
- One segment carries one MSS. In every worked example in this course the MSS is 1,200 bytes.
- The initial window (IW) is 2 segments. Older textbooks start from 1 and many current servers start from 10; we use 2 so the arithmetic stays small.
- Time is counted in rounds. One round is one RTT: send a window, collect its ACKs.
- The receiver window is assumed large enough never to matter.

### Slide 3. Slow start

- Begin at IW. Every ACK grows cwnd by one segment, so cwnd doubles each round.
- Slow to start, not slow to grow. The name compares it with what senders did before 1988: open with the whole receiver window at once.
- Slow start ends when cwnd reaches ssthresh or when a loss is detected, whichever comes first.
- Clamp rule: slow start never overshoots the threshold. Next cwnd = min(2 x cwnd, ssthresh).

Presenter remarks: they always assume slow start is the cautious phase. It is the aggressive one. Say it twice.

### Slide 4. Congestion avoidance

- At or above ssthresh: additive increase, +1.
- The sender is now feeling for spare capacity instead of racing towards it.
- ssthresh is the sender's memory of roughly where trouble began last time.
- The sender stays in this phase until a loss signal arrives.

### Slide 5. Loss signals

- Mild signal: three duplicate ACKs. One segment went missing but later ones are still getting through.
- After three duplicate ACKs: set ssthresh = cwnd / 2, then cwnd = ssthresh, and carry on in congestion avoidance.
- Severe signal: the retransmission timer expires. Nothing is getting through.
- After a timeout: set ssthresh = cwnd / 2, then cwnd = IW, and go back to slow start.
- Halves are rounded down, and ssthresh is never set below 2 segments.
- Course simplification: full Reno briefly inflates the window by 3 segments during fast recovery. We skip that step. In CNW 2140 the window lands on the new ssthresh in one move.

### Slide 6. The lecture 7 trace

Setup: IW = 2 segments, initial ssthresh = 16 segments, MSS = 1,200 bytes, RTT = 80 ms.

- Round 1: cwnd = 2 (slow start)
- Round 2: cwnd = 4 (slow start)
- Round 3: cwnd = 8 (slow start)
- Round 4: cwnd = 16 (slow start reaches ssthresh)
- Round 5: cwnd = 17 (congestion avoidance)
- Round 6: cwnd = 18
- Round 7: cwnd = 19
- Round 8: cwnd = 20; three duplicate ACKs arrive in this round
- Round 9: cwnd = 10, ssthresh = 10 (congestion avoidance continues)
- Round 10: cwnd = 11
- Round 11: cwnd = 12; the retransmission timer expires in this round
- Round 12: cwnd = 2, ssthresh = 6 (slow start again)
- Round 13: cwnd = 4
- Round 14: cwnd = 6 (clamped, because doubling would overshoot)
- Round 15: cwnd = 7 (congestion avoidance)

Lab 3 starts from this trace and asks you to extend it by ten rounds.

### Slide 7. Average throughput of the sawtooth

- In steady state the window swings between W / 2 and W, where W is the window at which loss occurs.
- The average window is therefore 0.75 x W.
- Formula used in this course: throughput = 0.75 x W x MSS / RTT.
- Slide example: W = 20 segments, MSS = 1,200 bytes, RTT = 80 ms. Average window 15 segments, 18,000 bytes per round, 225,000 bytes per second, which is 1.8 Mbit/s.
- We do not use the square-root loss formula (Mathis and colleagues) in this course. It is on the further reading list only.

### Slide 8. The retransmission timer

- Smoothed RTT: SRTT = 7/8 x SRTT + 1/8 x sample.
- Variation: RTTVAR = 3/4 x RTTVAR + 1/4 x the absolute difference between SRTT and the sample.
- Timeout value: RTO = SRTT + 4 x RTTVAR.
- Slide example: SRTT = 80 ms and RTTVAR = 15 ms give RTO = 140 ms.
- Each time the timer expires, the RTO doubles (exponential backoff).
- Course convention: in exercises we ignore the 1-second minimum RTO that real stacks apply.

### Slide 9. Why additive increase, multiplicative decrease

- Two flows sharing one bottleneck drift towards equal shares: both add the same amount, but the larger one loses more when both halve.
- Picture to remember: the staircase and the cliff. Climb one step per round; fall half the height on a loss.
- AIMD is fair.
- A sender that ignores the rules gains in the short term and wrecks the path for everyone, itself included.

### Slide 10. Before Thursday

- Lecture 8: TCP reliability and retransmission.
- Reading: Halloway and Minch, Networks from the Wire Up, sections 6.3 to 6.5.
- Bring a laptop with the capture tool installed for the lab session.

# CNW 2140 Computer Networks: lecturer's notes, weeks 3 and 4

Dr. Oleska Brantigern. These are my own running notes for lectures 5 to 7, posted after each session. They fill in what I said aloud and correct anything I said too loosely. They do not replace the slides.

Last edited: Wednesday 30 September 2026.

## Lecture 5 (Tuesday 22 September 2026): DNS

All term we resolve the same name: portal.tarnhollow.example.

The cast, in the order a lookup meets them:

1. The stub resolver on your laptop. It sends one recursive query and waits.
2. The campus recursive resolver at 10.40.0.53. It does the legwork iteratively.
3. A root server, which refers the resolver to the servers for .example.
4. The .example TLD server, which refers it to the zone's own name server.
5. The authoritative server for the zone, ns1.tarnhollow.example, which holds the record.

**How we count.** A cold lookup, with nothing cached anywhere, costs 4 queries in CNW 2140: laptop to campus resolver, resolver to root, resolver to TLD, resolver to authoritative. Several textbooks give 8 for the same exchange because they count the replies as well. We count queries only. If an exam wants messages rather than queries, it will say so.

**The record in the example.** The authoritative server returns an A record, 203.0.113.48, with a TTL of 300 seconds. In the lecture I said "think five minutes" and a few of you wrote that down as a property of DNS. It is not. The 300 seconds belongs to this one record and was chosen by whoever runs the zone. In the same example the NS records for tarnhollow.example carry a TTL of 86,400 seconds, a full day.

**Warm lookups.** While the A record is still within its TTL the campus resolver replies from its cache: 1 query from the laptop, none upstream. Once the A record has expired but the NS records are still cached, the resolver skips the root and the TLD and goes straight to ns1.

**Names that do not exist.** A reply of NXDOMAIN is cached too. In our zone the negative-caching time is 900 seconds, taken from the SOA record.

**The alias.** www.tarnhollow.example is a CNAME pointing at portal.tarnhollow.example. In our example it costs no extra query, because the same authoritative server holds both records and returns the CNAME and the A record in one reply. With the alias in a different zone you would pay for a second chain of referrals.

**"DNS is UDP."** I said this and it needs a footnote. Queries go to port 53 over UDP by default. If a reply would exceed 1,232 bytes (the limit we use in this course), the server sets the TC flag and the resolver repeats the query over TCP. Zone transfers between name servers always use TCP.

Housekeeping: the sandbox resolver for Lab 4 is at 10.40.0.54. Do not point your laptop at it for everyday use; it empties its cache every 60 seconds on purpose.

## Lecture 6 (Thursday 24 September 2026): HTTP

The page we load all term is the timetable page on the portal: one HTML file plus 11 embedded objects (8 images, 2 scripts, 1 stylesheet), so 12 objects in all.

**How we count round trips.** Opening a TCP connection costs 1 RTT. Each request with its response costs 1 RTT. We ignore TLS and we ignore transmission time until lecture 12. In the lecture the RTT was 50 ms.

- Non-persistent, one object at a time: every object pays for its own connection, 2 RTT each. Twelve objects make 24 RTT, which is 1,200 ms.
- Persistent, no pipelining: one handshake, then one round trip per object. That is 13 RTT, or 650 ms.
- Parallel non-persistent connections: the browser fetches the HTML first, on its own connection, then opens up to 6 connections at a time for the embedded objects. Each batch costs 2 RTT. I left the total for you to work out before the lab.

**Status codes in the demo.** The short address /tt replied 301 Moved Permanently and sent us to /timetable. The second load of the stylesheet replied 304 Not Modified, because the browser sent If-None-Match with the ETag "v7-a41c" and the file had not changed. I also showed a 503 from enrolment week, when the portal was overloaded.

**Caching.** The stylesheet carries Cache-Control: max-age=600, so for ten minutes the browser does not even ask. After that it revalidates with the ETag.

**"HTTP is stateless, full stop."** Too strong. The protocol is stateless: the server is not required to remember anything between two requests. The portal still knows who you are because your browser sends the sid cookie back with every request. The state lives in the cookie and in the server's session store, not in HTTP itself.

**HTTP/2 and later.** HTTP/2 multiplexes many streams over one connection, which removes the 6-connection juggling, but one lost TCP segment still stalls every stream. HTTP/3 over QUIC is lecture 12 and will not be on the midterm.

## Follow-ups from lecture 7 (TCP congestion control), added 30 September

**"+1" on the congestion avoidance slide.** Plus one segment per round, meaning per RTT. Not per ACK. Per ACK the growth is 1/cwnd of a segment, which adds up to one segment once a whole window has been acknowledged.

**"The window is 20."** In the throughput example, 20 is the peak: the window at which the loss happens. It is not the average and it is not the starting value.

**"AIMD is fair."** Fair between flows with similar round-trip times. A flow with a shorter RTT climbs its staircase more often and ends up with the larger share.

**Midterm scope.** The midterm covers everything up to and including lecture 7. Lecture 8 will be examined in the final only.

# ECN 1620 Prices, Markets and Money

## Lecture 5: Inflation and monetary policy

Prof. Tobiah Kessandru, Department of Economics, Tarnhollow University

Wednesday 30 September 2026

---

### Slide 1. Plan for today

- What inflation is, and what it is not
- How we measure it: the student basket
- Where it comes from
- What a central bank can do about it, and how long that takes

Our running case all term is the small open economy of Norvale: currency the crown, central bank the Norvale Reserve Board (NRB).

### Slide 2. The definition used in ECN 1620

- Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level.
- Sustained, in this course, means lasting at least two consecutive quarters. A one-off jump in prices is a price-level shock, not inflation.
- General means the basket as a whole. One price going up is a relative price change.
- Bands we use: mild is below 3% a year; moderate is 3% to below 10% a year; high is 10% a year or more; hyperinflation is 50% a month or more.

### Slide 3. Measuring it: the Norvale student basket

- Monthly basket, base year 2024: rent 700, food 300, transport 90, phone and data 60, books 100. Total 1,250 crowns.
- The same basket cost 1,300 crowns in 2025 and 1,365 crowns in 2026.
- CPI: 100.0 in 2024, 104.0 in 2025, 109.2 in 2026.
- Inflation in 2026 is 5.0%: the rise from 104.0 to 109.2, divided by 104.0.
- Always measure from the previous year's index, not from the base year.
- In this course inflation means CPI inflation unless a problem says GDP deflator.

### Slide 4. Where it comes from

- Demand-pull: spending outruns what the economy can produce. Our example: the 2021 Norvale housing grant.
- Cost-push: production gets more expensive. Our example: the 2023 Port Selby harbour strike, which raised the cost of everything imported.
- Expectations: if firms and workers expect 5%, they set prices and wages to match, and 5% is what they get.
- "Inflation is always and everywhere a monetary phenomenon." Discuss.

### Slide 5. Money and prices

- Quantity equation: M x V = P x Y.
- Growth form: money growth + velocity growth = inflation + real output growth.
- Norvale example: the money supply grows 7%, velocity is flat, real output grows 2%. Predicted inflation: 5%.

### Slide 6. Nominal and real

- Real rate = nominal rate - inflation. This is the approximation; use it whenever inflation is below 10%.
- At 10% or more, use the exact form: (1 + nominal) = (1 + real) x (1 + inflation).
- Example: a Norvale savings account pays 3.5%. With inflation at 5.0%, the saver's real return is -1.5%.
- Real rates are negative right now.

### Slide 7. The Norvale Reserve Board

- Inflation target: 2%.
- Policy rate today: 4.25%.
- The Board meets 8 times a year.
- Tools: the policy rate (the main one), open market operations, the reserve requirement (8% in Norvale), forward guidance.

### Slide 8. The classroom rule

- policy rate = neutral real rate + inflation + 0.5 x (inflation - target) + 0.25 x output gap
- In ECN 1620 we use a neutral real rate of 1% and a target of 2%.
- This is a Taylor-type rule with our own weights. Taylor's 1993 paper used different numbers. In ECN 1620 exams, use the classroom weights.
- Norvale today: inflation 5.0%, output gap -2%. The rule gives 1 + 5 + 1.5 - 0.5 = 7.0%.
- The NRB is behind the curve.

### Slide 9. How policy reaches prices

- Four channels: the interest-rate channel, the credit channel, the exchange-rate channel, the expectations channel.
- Lags: borrowing responds within 1 to 2 quarters. Our rule of thumb for the full effect on inflation is 6 quarters.
- So a rate decision today is aimed at inflation a year and a half from now.

### Slide 10. Banks and the multiplier

- Money multiplier = 1 / reserve ratio. With Norvale's 8% that is 12.5.
- Example: 200 crowns of new reserves can support up to 2,500 crowns of deposits.
- In practice banks hold excess reserves and households hold cash, so the real multiplier is smaller.

### Slide 11. Why we care

- Shoe-leather costs: time and effort spent holding less cash.
- Menu costs: the expense of changing prices often.
- Unexpected inflation moves wealth from lenders to borrowers.
- Deflation is not the cure. Falling prices make debts heavier and persuade buyers to wait.

### Slide 12. Next week

- Lecture 6, Wednesday 7 October: unemployment and the Phillips curve.
- Reading: Kessandru and Ilves, Money in Small Economies, chapter 9.
- Problem set 3 is due Wednesday 14 October.
