# Brindlewatch Fit: Installation Service Guide

Version 3.0 | Effective 17 August 2026
Owner: Wilhelmina Castellanos-Reid, Fit Programme Lead | Approved by: Odalys Ferreira-Novak, Director of Customer Care
For Customer Care agents at every tier | Read with the Fit Service Areas sheet for the current month

## 1. What Fit is

Fit is a paid home visit. An installer mounts the customer's cameras, connects them and checks the view with the customer before leaving. It is available for Lantern Cam and Eave Cam, wherever the camera was bought. Trek Cam is a portable camera and is not part of Fit.

The visits are carried out by two partner companies, Thornapple Home Services and Kestrel & Vane Installations. Installers are employed by the partner, not by Brindlewatch. Each carries a Fit badge with their name and the booking reference, and the customer is entitled to see it before letting anyone in.

Fit is a stand-alone service. A customer does not need a Keep plan to book it, and the price does not change with the plan.

Fit is a service for homes. Shops, offices and other business premises are not booked through the Fit calendar; those enquiries go to the Brindlewatch for Business team. In a flat or a rented home, getting permission for fixings on a wall the customer does not own is the customer's job, and the installer will ask whether it has been given before drilling.

## 2. Prices

| Item | Price |
|---|---|
| First camera in a visit | $95 |
| Every additional camera in the same visit | $55 |
| High mount: a camera fixed more than 12 feet above the ground | $24 on top, for that camera |
| Travel fee, outer-ring areas only | The amount shown against the area in the Fit Service Areas sheet, once for the visit |

Prices are before sales tax. A visit covers up to 8 cameras; a larger job is booked as two visits, and each visit is priced from the first camera again. The full amount is paid at booking, by card or digital wallet. A receipt for the visit is e-mailed with the confirmation and is separate from any invoice for a plan.

A visit is priced by the cameras fitted, not by the time it takes. Agents do not estimate how long an installer will be at the address.

## 3. Booking a visit

Agents book in the Fit calendar in the support console. The calendar offers only the days on which the partner works in the customer's area, and no day earlier than the area's earliest slot. In the Fit Service Areas sheet, the earliest-slot figure is the number of calendar days between the day of booking and the first day that can be offered.

The customer chooses one of three arrival windows: 8 am to 11 am, 11 am to 2 pm, or 2 pm to 5 pm. The window is when the installer arrives, not when the work is finished.

A confirmation is e-mailed with a booking reference beginning FIT-. A reminder is e-mailed on the day before the visit.

The cameras have to be at the address before the installer arrives. A visit can be booked while an order is still on its way, as long as the first day offered is later than the end of the delivery estimate.

Someone aged 18 or over has to be at the address throughout the visit.

Before the visit. When booking, read the customer the short list the installer depends on: the name and password of the home network to hand, the Brindlewatch app already on a phone and signed in, a clear path to each spot where a camera is going, and pets kept in another room. The installer does not need to be told the network password; the customer types it in.

Adding a camera. A camera can be added to a booked visit, at the additional-camera price, at any time up to the cut-off for free changes in section 4. After the cut-off the installer fits what was booked and no more.

For an area marked Planned in the sheet, say that Fit is not available there yet. Give an opening date only when the sheet shows one that is marked as announced.

## 4. Changing or cancelling

| Situation | What happens |
|---|---|
| Customer changes or cancels 36 hours or more before the start of the arrival window | No fee. For a cancelled visit the full amount goes back to the customer |
| Customer cancels less than 36 hours before the start of the arrival window | A $40 late cancellation fee is kept and the rest is refunded |
| Customer asks to move the visit less than 36 hours before the start of the arrival window | Treated as a late cancellation followed by a new booking |
| Nobody aged 18 or over is at the address | The installer waits 20 minutes, then records a missed visit. The same $40 fee is kept and the rest is refunded |
| The cameras have not been delivered | The visit is moved at no fee, whatever the notice. Check the order status before moving it |
| The partner cancels (weather, illness, vehicle) | The customer chooses a new slot or gets the full amount back. Nothing further is owed |

A Tier 1 agent cannot waive the late cancellation fee. The agent can submit a waiver request to the Fit Programme desk, tells the customer that the desk decides, and does not say what the desk will decide.

## 5. On the day

What the installer does:

- fixes the mount with the fixings supplied, on brick, timber, siding or render;
- for a Lantern Cam, runs the supplied cable to the nearest existing outlet;
- connects the camera to the customer's account on the customer's own phone, with the customer signed in;
- checks the view with the customer and adjusts the angle;
- takes the packaging away.

What the installer does not do:

- fit new electrical outlets or alter house wiring;
- work on a roof, or fix a camera more than 20 feet above the ground;
- fit cameras or mounts from other makers;
- take down or dispose of equipment that is already there;
- ask for the customer's password, sign in to the account, or keep any access to it afterwards.

An installer cannot help with plans, bills or the account. Customers who raise those on the day are asked to contact Customer Care.

## 6. Workmanship guarantee

The mounting work is guaranteed for 1 year from the day of the visit. If a mount works loose or a fixing fails in that time, the partner returns and puts it right at no charge. The guarantee covers the installer's work. It does not cover the camera, which falls under the Repair and Replacement Service Terms, and it does not cover a camera the customer has since moved.

## 7. When a fitted camera is returned

A camera fitted under Fit can still be returned under the Refund and Cancellation Policy, and the refund for the camera follows that policy without change. The Fit charge for that camera is a different matter:

- if the visit has not taken place, the full Fit charge is refunded;
- if the visit has taken place, the Fit charge for that camera is refunded less a $35 call-out charge;
- a high-mount amount or a travel fee is not refunded once the visit has taken place.

The customer takes the camera down. Fit does not offer a removal visit.

## 8. Damage to the property

Damage the customer believes the installer caused - a cracked tile, a marked wall - is reported to Customer Care with the booking reference. The agent logs it for the Fit Programme desk, which passes it to the partner. The partner's insurer deals with the customer directly. Agents do not accept liability, do not offer payment and do not estimate what the partner will do.

## 9. What agents say

- Quote from section 2 and from the current sheet, and nowhere else.
- Give the arrival window as a window. Do not promise a time inside it, and do not promise a particular installer.
- Read the cut-off for free changes and the late cancellation fee to the customer before taking payment.
- Do not describe the installer as a Brindlewatch employee.

## 10. The Fit Programme desk

The Fit Programme desk handles waiver requests, complaints about a visit, partner cancellations and anything the sheet does not answer. It works on weekdays, 9 am to 6 pm Central, and is reached through the Fit category in the support console. It replies by the end of the next business day.

## Revision history

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 3.0 | 17 August 2026 | Single national price list; cut-off for free changes set at 36 hours; late fee revised; pilot rules withdrawn |
| 2.1 | 13 April 2026 | Kestrel & Vane Installations added as second partner |
| 2.0 | 1 April 2026 | Fit opened beyond the two pilot areas |
texts.CC-REF-FIT-PILOT-2025:
BRINDLEWATCH FIT - PILOT BRIEFING FOR CUSTOMER CARE

Issued 10 November 2025
From: Wilhelmina Castellanos-Reid, Fit Pilot Lead
To: all Tier 1 agents and Team Leads
Pilot period: 24 November 2025 to 31 March 2026


WHAT IS HAPPENING

From 24 November we are trying out a home installation service under the name Brindlewatch Fit. An installer visits the customer, puts the cameras up and makes sure they are working before leaving. Customers have been asking for this since the Eave Cam launched, and the pilot is how we find out whether we can offer it at a sensible price and to a standard we are happy with.

The pilot is small on purpose. Please read the limits below before you offer it to anyone.


WHERE

Two areas only: Harrowmere and Dunmere Heights. The console will not let you book an address anywhere else. If a customer outside those two areas asks, say that the service is being tried in a small number of places and is not available where they live yet. Do not suggest when it might be.


WHO DOES THE WORK

One partner, Thornapple Home Services. Their installers have been trained on Lantern Cam and Eave Cam at our offices. They carry a Thornapple identity card; there is no Brindlewatch badge during the pilot.


PILOT PRICES

  First camera in a visit ............... $69
  Every additional camera, same visit ... $39

A visit covers up to 4 cameras. There is no high-mount work in the pilot: installers will not fix anything more than 10 feet above the ground, and there is no travel fee because both areas are close to the Thornapple depots.

The full amount is taken when you book.

Please do not describe the pilot prices as an introductory offer or suggest that they will last. They were set to find out what customers will pay, and they may go up or down.


BOOKING

Book in the Fit calendar (new tab in the console, visible from 24 November). There are two arrival windows during the pilot, a morning one from 8 am to 12 noon and an afternoon one from 12 noon to 5 pm. Visits run on weekdays only.

The customer gets a confirmation by e-mail. Thornapple also telephones the customer on the working day before the visit to confirm.

The cameras must already be at the address when you book. During the pilot we are not booking visits against orders that are still on their way, because a late parcel wastes a crew's half day.


HOW TO BRING IT UP

Offer Fit when a customer in one of the two areas tells you they are not confident putting a camera up, or asks whether we know someone who can. Do not offer it on every contact from those areas, and do not offer it on a contact about a fault or a complaint. One sentence is enough: we are trying out a fitting service where they live, this is what it costs, would they like a visit. If they say no, leave it there.


CHANGES AND CANCELLATIONS DURING THE PILOT

The customer can move or cancel a visit free of charge until 6 pm on the day before it. After 6 pm on the day before, or if nobody is in when the installer calls, a $20 late fee is kept and the rest goes back to the customer.

Team Leads can waive the late fee during the pilot where they think it is fair. Agents cannot.


IF THE CUSTOMER SENDS THE CAMERA BACK

During the pilot, when a camera fitted by us is returned inside the normal return period, the entire Fit charge for that camera goes back to the customer along with the camera's price. We will look at this again once we know how often it happens.


GUARANTEE

Thornapple guarantee their mounting work for 6 months. If a customer reports a loose mount in that time, book a return visit in the calendar under the label REFIX; there is no charge and the visit does not count towards the pilot numbers.


WHAT THE INSTALLER WILL AND WILL NOT DO

Will: fix the mount, connect the camera on the customer's phone, check the view with the customer.

Will not: touch house wiring, go on a roof, fit other makes of camera, or deal with anything to do with the customer's plan or bill. Please make that last point clear when you book, because the installers have been getting asked.


WHAT WE ARE MEASURING

- Visits completed: the aim is 400 across the two areas by the end of March.
- Share of visits finished inside the arrival window.
- Customers' rating of the visit, from a short survey e-mailed the next morning.
- How many cameras fitted under Fit come back, compared with cameras customers fit themselves.

You do not need to collect any of this. It comes from the calendar and the survey.


WHAT TO NOTE ON THE CONTACT

Put FIT PILOT at the start of your notes on any contact where the service was offered, whether or not the customer booked. It is how we count interest.


WHERE TO SEND THINGS

Anything the calendar will not let you do, any complaint about a visit, and any request from a customer outside the two areas who is insistent: the pilot mailbox, fitpilot@brindlewatch.example. It is read on weekdays and you should have an answer the same day.


AFTER THE PILOT

The pilot ends on 31 March 2026. Prices, the number of cameras in a visit, the cancellation rule and the areas will all be looked at again before anything is offered more widely, and nothing in this briefing should be read as what the service will look like afterwards. A fuller guide will take the place of this briefing if the service continues.

# Customer Care Quality Scorecard Guide

Version 1.4 | Effective 28 September 2026
Owner: Leocadia Brannigan-Oyelaran, Quality Lead | Approved by: Odalys Ferreira-Novak, Director of Customer Care
Applies to: Tier 1 contacts by phone and by chat

## 1. Why contacts are reviewed

Reviews exist so that a customer gets the same correct answer whoever picks up. A scorecard is a record of one contact measured against the documents that were current on the day of that contact. It is not a measure of how pleasant the customer was, how long the contact took or how the agent's month is going.

This guide tells agents what a reviewer listens for, how the points are shared out, and what to do when a score looks wrong.

## 2. Which contacts are reviewed

The quality tool picks contacts at random.

| Agent | Contacts reviewed in a calendar month |
|---|---|
| Agent past their first 12 weeks | 6 |
| Agent in their first 12 weeks | 10 |

For an agent who works both channels, at least 1 of the contacts picked is a chat. Contacts shorter than 60 seconds are left out, and so are contacts that were transferred in from another agent.

A Team Lead can add a contact to the month's reviews when a customer has complained about it. An added contact is scored in the same way and counts towards the month.

Chat contacts are scored on the same scorecard. Where an agent was handling more than one chat at once, the reviewer reads only the chat that was picked, and a slow reply caused by the other chat is not marked down under Communication.

## 3. The scorecard

| Section | Points | What the reviewer checks |
|---|---|---|
| Verification and account safety | 25 | The right checks for this caller and this action, completed before anything specific to the account was said or done |
| Accuracy | 30 | Prices, fees, time limits and rules given as the current documents state them; required statements made (section 5) |
| Ownership | 20 | The agent dealt with what Tier 1 can deal with, handed on what it cannot, and chose the right team |
| Communication | 15 | Plain words, an even pace, no talking over the customer, and a clear account of the next step |
| Record keeping | 10 | Notes that let the next colleague carry on without asking the customer to start again |

The sections add up to 100. A contact passes at 85 or above. The agent's monthly score is the plain average of the contacts reviewed that month.

Accuracy deductions. Each wrong price, fee, time limit or rule stated to the customer takes 10 points off the Accuracy section, until the section reaches zero. An error the agent puts right before the contact ends costs nothing. Saying "let me confirm that" and then confirming it is never an error.

## 4. Automatic fails

Five things set the score for the entire contact to 0, whatever else happened on it:

- an action on an account, or a disclosure from it, made without the verification that the Account Verification Standard requires for that action, including step-up verification that was needed and skipped;
- a promise of an outcome that is somebody else's to decide;
- personal details read out or confirmed to a person who is not entitled to them;
- mockery or abuse of a customer;
- a note that records something which did not happen.

An automatic fail is looked at by a second reviewer before it is published, and it still counts as one contact in the monthly average.

## 5. Required statements

On some kinds of contact the customer has to hear particular things. Each one that is missing takes 5 points off the Accuracy section.

| Kind of contact | The customer must hear |
|---|---|
| Quote for a repair outside the warranty | The flat fee for that model; that the quote stays open for 15 calendar days; that the camera comes back unrepaired if the quote is not taken up |
| Advance exchange offered | That a hold goes on the card, and what releases it |
| Fit visit booked | The price of the visit as booked; the cut-off for changing it free of charge; the late cancellation fee |
| Case handed to another team | What the Escalation Matrix says the customer is told |
| Refund passed up for a decision | What the Refund and Cancellation Policy says the customer is told |

Reviewers do not listen for set wording. The statement counts if the customer could have understood it.

## 6. Keeping reviewers in step

Every second Wednesday the reviewers and the Team Leads each score the same 4 contacts without conferring. Any score that sits more than 5 points away from the Quality Lead's reference score is talked through, and the reference is changed when the room agrees it was wrong. Notes from each session are posted in the Customer Care channel, and agents are welcome to read them.

A reviewer never scores a contact handled by a member of their own household or by someone who reports to them.

## 7. Publishing and coaching

Scorecards are published in the quality tool each Friday for the contacts reviewed that week. Each one shows the points by section, the reviewer's comments and time markers for the parts of the contact the comments refer to.

- A contact below 85 is followed by a coaching conversation with the agent's Team Lead within 12 calendar days of publication.
- A monthly score below 85 in 2 consecutive months leads to a support plan agreed between the agent and the Team Lead, reviewed after 8 weeks.
- A monthly score of 95 or above for three months running makes an agent eligible to sit in on the Wednesday sessions as a guest scorer.

Coaching is a conversation about one contact. It is not a disciplinary step, and nothing in this guide sets pay.

Agents in their first 12 weeks. Scores from the first 4 weeks on live contacts are shown to the agent and the Team Lead but are left out of every average. From week 5 the scores count, and the pass mark is the same as for everyone else.

## 8. Disputing a score

An agent who thinks a score is wrong raises a dispute in the quality tool within 8 calendar days of the scorecard being published, naming the section and giving the reason. The reason has to point to a document: "the policy says otherwise" with the section number is a reason, "the customer was happy" is not.

The Quality Lead, or a reviewer who did not score the contact, decides no later than 6 business days after the dispute is raised. If the dispute is upheld the scorecard is corrected and the monthly average recalculated. There is one dispute for each contact and the decision is final.

A dispute against an automatic fail is decided by the Quality Lead in person.

## 9. What the scorecard leaves out

- Handle time and the number of contacts taken. Workforce reporting covers those and they do not move a quality score in either direction.
- Whether the customer bought anything. Offering a plan or a Fit visit earns no points, and not offering one loses none.
- The customer's own rating of the contact. Survey results are reported next to quality scores, never blended into them.

## 10. Points that come up again and again

- Being marked down for something that changed. A contact is scored against the documents in force on the day it took place. If a figure changed the following week, the old figure was still the right one to give.
- Customers who would not let the agent verify them. Ending the contact politely without touching the account scores full points for Verification and account safety.
- Handing on. Passing a case to the right team at the right moment is scored under Ownership as a good outcome, not as a failure to resolve.
- Silence while working. Reviewers do not take points for quiet stretches as long as the customer was told what the agent was doing.

## 11. Recordings used for review

Call recordings and chat transcripts held for review are kept for 120 days and then removed from the quality tool. Reviewers can open only the contacts the tool has assigned to them. A contact that is the subject of an open dispute is held until the dispute is decided.

## Revision history

| Version | Date | Change |
|---|---|---|
| 1.4 | 28 September 2026 | Required statements added for repair quotes, advance exchange and Fit visits |
| 1.3 | 11 May 2026 | Pass mark raised from 80 to 85; guest scorers introduced |
| 1.2 | 19 January 2026 | Chat contacts brought into the monthly reviews |

# Device Service and Fit: monthly report for Customer Care

September 2026 | Issued 5 October 2026
Prepared by Florentyn Akabueze-Marsh (Device Service) and Wilhelmina Castellanos-Reid (Fit Programme)
Circulation: Customer Care Team Leads and Tier 1 agents. Figures are for the calendar month unless a line says otherwise. This report describes what happened; it sets no rule, and the service terms and guides remain the place to look for those.

## 1. Headlines

- 1,312 units were scanned in at Marrow Creek, against 1,187 in August. The rise is almost all Eave Cam.
- Dispatch targets were met on 96.4% of standard exchanges and 91.8% of paid repairs.
- Fit partners completed 2,046 visits. Greyling Ford and Yarrowby opened during the month; Brackwater was paused on 28 September.
- The second inspection, new on 1 September, was requested 9 times.

## 2. Claims by route and camera

| Camera | Standard exchange | Advance exchange | Paid repair | All routes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Lantern Cam | 318 | 61 | 142 | 521 |
| Eave Cam | 402 | 97 | 118 | 617 |
| Trek Cam | 88 | 23 | 63 | 174 |
| All cameras | 808 | 181 | 323 | 1,312 |

Accessory exchanges are raised by Tier 1 and do not pass through the bench, so they are not in this table. There were 409 of them, most often a power adapter.

## 3. Bench outcomes

| Outcome | Units | Share |
|---|---|---|
| Fault confirmed | 1,021 | 77.8% |
| No fault found | 148 | 11.3% |
| Customer damage found on a claim inside the warranty | 96 | 7.3% |
| Could not be repaired; renewed unit supplied | 47 | 3.6% |

No fault found. In most of these the camera joined the bench network at the first attempt, which points to the home network and not to the unit. Eleven cameras came back for a second no-fault-found return and carried the handling charge.

Second inspections. Of the 9 requested, 5 upheld the first report, 2 overturned it and 2 were still pending when the month closed. Both overturned reports involved hairline marks on an Eave Cam housing that the second technician judged to be moulding marks.

Repeat faults. The Head of Device Service reviewed 4 cameras that had already been exchanged twice for the same fault code. All 4 were Trek Cams from one production batch, and Tier 2 has been told which batch.

## 4. Dispatch performance

| Measure | Target | September | August |
|---|---|---|---|
| Standard exchange: replacement dispatched after scan-in | 4 business days | average 2.6 | average 3.1 |
| Paid repair: unit dispatched after payment | 9 business days | average 6.2 | average 7.4 |
| Advance exchange: faulty unit scanned in after the replacement left | 20 calendar days | average 11.5 | average 12.2 |

Paid repairs missed the target mostly in the second week, when a delivery of Trek Cam lens assemblies arrived late. Of 181 advance-exchange holds, 7 became a charge because the faulty unit was never sent in.

Repair quotes. 323 quotes were sent. 271 were accepted and paid, 38 lapsed and the units went back unrepaired, and 14 were still open at the end of the month.

## 5. Where agents can help

- 63 parcels arrived with accessories in the box. They cannot be matched back to a customer once the camera has gone to the bench. Please keep telling customers to send the camera only.
- 29 parcels arrived with no Return Authorisation number on the label and went back to the sender unopened.
- 112 claims waited for proof of purchase before they could move. They sat for an average of 3.4 days. Asking for the order number or the receipt on the first contact removes most of that wait.
- Notes marked for the Device Service desk were answered by the end of the next business day in all but 6 cases.

## 6. Contacts about open claims

Tier 1 took 2,874 contacts from customers with a claim open, about 2.2 for every unit scanned in.

| Reason for the contact | Share |
|---|---|
| Where the unit or the replacement has got to | 41% |
| The repair quote: what it covers, how to pay | 22% |
| A card hold that the customer expected to have gone | 9% |
| Disagreement with a bench outcome | 6% |
| Everything else | 22% |

On card holds: the desk releases a hold on the day the faulty unit is scanned in, but the customer's bank decides when the release shows on a statement. Agents can see the release date on the claim record and can give the customer that date.

## 7. Fit

| Partner | Visits completed | Arrived inside the window | Missed visits | Late cancellations |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Thornapple Home Services | 1,283 | 94.1% | 31 | 58 |
| Kestrel & Vane Installations | 763 | 89.7% | 27 | 44 |
| Both partners | 2,046 | 92.5% | 58 | 102 |

The 2,046 visits fitted 4,410 cameras, about 2.2 a visit; 388 of those cameras were high mounts.

Kestrel & Vane's arrival figure was pulled down by Cinder Bluff and Yarrowby, where one crew covers long distances. The partner is adding a second vehicle in Sablecrest.

Late fee. The Fit Programme desk received 37 waiver requests and granted 12, nearly all where a customer had been taken into hospital or a parcel had been misrouted. A request with the reason written out is decided faster than one that says only that the customer is unhappy.

Workmanship. Partners returned to 19 addresses under the guarantee, most often for a mount on render that had worked loose.

Property. 6 reports of damage were passed to the partners. None has been closed yet.

Returns. 71 cameras fitted under Fit were sent back for a refund during the month, out of roughly 4,400 fitted.

## 8. Coming up

- The October issue of the Fit Service Areas sheet went out on 1 October. Please stop using the September issue.
- The bench at Marrow Creek closes for a stock count on Friday 30 October. Units are still scanned in that day, and the day does not count towards the dispatch targets.
- A second label printer goes in at the service centre in November, which should end the start-of-week backlog of outbound parcels.
